verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.118889 did not improve on the current best 1.067101 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: The 50M baseline was undertrained in the 5-minute budget, so scaling up to a larger model reduced tokens per parameter and hurt val_bpb; the first scaling experiment should shrink the model instead.

judge.summary: The agent kept the current best model size direction but took one more shrink step: it edited train.py to set DEPTH = 4 instead of DEPTH = 5, which also reduced the derived embedding dimension from 384 to 256. It committed this one-line change and ran the experiment. The run completed successfully, but the model only used 11.5M parameters, trained 831M tokens, and produced val_bpb = 1.118889, much worse than the current best 1.067101, so it was not an improvement.
judge.feedback: The decisive mistake was the experiment choice at the point where DEPTH was changed from 5 to 4. The previous successful shrink from depth 8 to 5 showed that the depth-8 model was undertrained, but the depth-5 / n_embd-384 model is already near the capacity floor for this 5-minute budget. Dropping to depth 4 / n_embd 256 reduced the parameter count from 24.6M to 11.5M, and although it trained more tokens, the loss increase from undercapacity dominated, giving a large regression. A better next step would have been to keep the current model size and probe an orthogonal training hyperparameter, for example reducing the LR warmdown fraction so that more of the fixed time budget is spent at useful high LR instead of decaying to zero for half the run.
judge.corrected_step: WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.2    # fraction of time budget for LR warmdown
judge.hint: Do not shrink below the current depth-5 model; the size direction has bottomed out, so try a training-schedule change such as a shorter warmdown instead.
